sources.label: Monerium issuer smart-contract repository: blacklist and token controls

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Monerium's issuer repository explicitly documents administrator blacklisting that prevents addresses from transferring or receiving tokens, shared between its tokens within a deployment environment. Its current Token.sol invokes an owner-selected validator before transfer and transferFrom. This supports the retained Yes review from a primary issuer disclosure rather than inference from centralized governance. On 2026-10-01, owner and implementation-slot reads across all six tracked GBPe deployments matched the recorded issuer-controlled owner paths. The public repository describes the control design; it is not an independently reproduced bytecode-to-source match for every historical v1/v2 deployment, nor a census of currently frozen holders. Failure domain is Monerium's token/validator administration, distinct from offchain safeguarding-provider failures.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Monerium issues GBPe natively on each supported chain; per-chain owner() reads (2026-07-20) resolve to Monerium owner Safes rather than bridge contracts. Cross-chain movement is issuer-native burn/mint through linked Monerium accounts, not a public third-party bridge.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-2 (lead usdc-circle)

Cross-chain movement is issuer-side burn/mint through Monerium accounts, so no external bridge custody carries the claim.
